target: new: two qualities of one bearer (asymmetrical PATO_0000616 + ovate FLOPO:0991024)
reason: Two qualities stated together: the outline is oval, and it is uneven (lopsided). Each has a term, so this is a pairing of two values, not a new term. In this lexicon 'oval' is a synonym of PATO ovate.
The costa or cell region is not clearly set off from the tissue around it. This is the same reading as the earlier rule 'indistinct' = inconspicuous (C175).

label: elimbate
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a leaf or leaf margin by virtue of the margin's not being bordered by a band of elongate or otherwise differentiated cells (a limbidium).
reason: A standard moss term. Neither PO nor FLOPO has a limbidium class, so an 'absent' rule has no part to point to. If a limbidium anatomy class is added later, this should become an entity_absence rule.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: oblong PATO_0000946 to ovate FLOPO:0991024)
reason: A compound of two shapes run together, like 'oblong-ovate'. It is handled as the continuum between the two values.
'Semi-' weakens leaf-like the same way 'sub-' does. It is the approximate-value pattern on PATO leaf-like.
'Clad in' means covered by persistent leaf sheaths or petiole bases. As with 'covered' (C240), the quality lies in what does the covering, not in the word itself.

label: triternate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a compound leaf by virtue of its being divided three times in succession into three parts, so that the ultimate leaflets are borne in groups of three.
reason: A standard term for divided leaves that no existing term covers. It follows tripinnate FLOPO:0991159 and trifoliolate FLOPO:0991161; 'ternate' and 'biternate' would be its siblings.
This says a part is absent, but neither PO nor FLOPO has a cystolith class (a mineral deposit inside a cell), so there is nothing to mark absent. A cystolith class needs to be requested first.
Finely hairy with gland-tipped hairs, which falls under glandular-pubescent (at least some hairs tipped with a gland). The 'very short hair' part of puberulent is lost.
The same term without the hyphen. It also applies to a fruit that develops from a half-inferior ovary.
'Somewhat stiff'. Stiff is an exact synonym of PATO inflexible, and '-ish' marks an approximate value.

label: stomatomorphic
definition: A shape quality inhering in a stigma by virtue of its two lips or lobes being pressed close together around a narrow slit, like the guard cells round the opening of a stoma.
reason: A real stigma type used in Gesneriaceae descriptions. PATO and FLOPO have no stigma shape that matches it.
Exserted only a little way. The quality is exserted, and 'short' only gives the degree.
'With trichomes' means hairy, and PATO has a term for that. 'Trichome present' would also be valid, but the quality term matches the other indumentum rules.
This means 'without an appendage', but 'appendage' was rejected earlier as a generic part, and no 'appendiculate' quality exists to negate.
A plant group or life form, not a quality of a plant part.
What 'flagged' means for a leaf is unclear without the source context, and there is no quality to negate.
'Like that of Corylus' (hazel): a shape defined by pointing to one genus, used for the involucre in a single group. It is too narrow and too tied to a taxon for a term.

label: pseudo-opposite
definition: An alternate placement quality inhering in structures by virtue of their being inserted singly at successive nodes so close together that they appear to be paired at one node.
reason: The leaves look opposite but are actually alternate, so this is not an approximate 'opposite'. It is a recognised arrangement (e.g. Solanaceae) with no term.
Squamate means covered with scales. Same reading as the earlier rule lepidote = scaly (C235).

target: cartilaginous (sensu botany) (FLOPO:0991099) on the margin of the bearer
reason: The margin is hard and thickened. That is cartilaginous (sensu botany), whose definition names the margin as its usual bearer; the margin goes in as the part of the bearer.
A peristome type named after a species. It means nothing without that comparison and is not a general quality.
Nearly always a count of cell layers ('2-stratose'). When no number is given it is PATO stratified (layered).

target: new: two qualities of one bearer (tomentose PATO_0002341 + sericeous PATO_0104358)
reason: Two hair types stated together, each with a PATO term. It is a compound of two values, not a new term.
'Hard-leaved'. When the whole plant is described, the bearer becomes the leaf.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (basiscopic side larger than acroscopic side)
reason: A comparison: the lower (base-facing) side of the pinna is larger than the upper side. Plain 'asymmetrical' would lose which side is larger.
'Almost hyaline' (nearly clear). Hyaline is a synonym of PATO transparent, and 'sub-' marks an approximate value.
No roots grow from the stem nodes. PO shoot-borne root (synonym adventitious root) is the missing part, and the stem node is where it would be.

label: basisolute
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's base being prolonged downward beyond its point of attachment as a free extension.
reason: A recognised term for bracts and bracteoles that has no PATO or FLOPO equivalent. It sits beside basifixed and dorsifixed as an attachment quality.

label: petiole-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a petiole, being narrow and stalk-like.
reason: Mostly a leaf base narrowed into a stalk without being a true petiole. It is a sibling of PATO leaf-like and FLOPO bract-like (FLOPO:0991200).
